transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yes, thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um... I hope I'm not overreacting by being here, to be honest. I know you probably see people with much more serious issues. 

I just came in because... well, I'm usually a very disciplined sleeper. I really have to be, to keep up with my schedule. But since my cousin died recently, I've just been having a bit of a hiccup with my rest. I'll lie awake sort of... replaying the night it happened. And then I end up waking up at 3 or 4 in the morning from these... just silly scraps of hospital images. 

It's a bit embarrassing, really, not being able to just switch it off. I go into my board meetings feeling like I’ve only slept in pieces. I mean, I push through it and get the work done, of course, but... I just want to get back to my normal routine and make sure I'm handling this the right way. Is... is it alright that I came in for something like this?
Have you been feeling sad or empty since your cousin's death?

Sad? Well, I mean, naturally, it's a very sad time for the family. But... I don't know if 'empty' is the exact word, I just... well, I hope this doesn't make me sound like a terrible person. I really don't want you to think I'm cold, because I'm usually very supportive. 

It's just that... during the prayer gatherings, and even when my nieces were trying so hard to comfort me, I found myself... well, I behaved properly, of course. I made sure to say all the right things and be strong for them. But I just didn't feel any warmth or relief inside. It was almost as if the affectionate part of me had just... gone a bit quiet. 

I feel quite guilty admitting that out loud, to be honest. I really do care for them deeply. It's just a temporary reaction to the shock, right? I hope it's normal that I'm responding this way...
How long have you felt like the affectionate part of you had gone quiet?

Well, it's been... about three weeks now. Ever since the night it happened. My cousin died in a highway collision, you see, and... I suppose ever since that night, things have just felt a bit muffled. 

But three weeks isn't really that long to be out of sorts, is it? I mean, I'm sure it's a perfectly standard timeline to still be adjusting after a sudden accident like that. I just want to make sure I'm not dragging this out longer than I should be, and that I'm handling it all the right way. It's okay that it's taking me a few weeks to bounce back, right?
Have you found yourself less interested in the things you normally enjoy since your cousin's death?

Less interested? Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I've really made it a point to keep up with my usual activities. I still go to my weekend tennis matches and, you know, host my usual dinner parties. 

I mean, I think it's so important to just keep pushing forward and stay engaged, don't you agree? I certainly don't want to be someone who just... wallows and stops living their life because things got difficult. So, no, I haven't lost interest at all. I make sure to stay just as active as before. That's a good sign, isn't it? That I'm still doing all the things I normally enjoy?
Have you been avoiding people, places, or activities that remind you of your cousin?

Avoiding things? Oh, no, I really haven't. I actually... well, I made sure to go over to his house just the other day to help his wife sort through some of the estate paperwork. I mean, it's the responsible thing to do, isn't it? 

I would absolutely hate for my family—or anyone, really—to think I was shrinking away from my duties just because it's a difficult situation. I've always believed you have to face these things head-on. So, no, I haven't been avoiding any places or people at all. I think it's much better to just keep showing up for the people who need you, don't you agree? I hope that shows I'm managing things reasonably well...
Do you feel guilty about something specific related to your cousin's death?

Guilty? Oh... no. No, I really don't. I mean, it was a highway collision, so it was completely out of anyone's hands. 

I've always prided myself on being a very practical person, and I know it wouldn't be at all productive to sit around blaming myself for something I couldn't control. I think it's much better to just focus my energy on what I can actually do now, like helping his wife with the estate. That's the healthiest way to look at it, don't you think? I certainly wouldn't want to invent reasons to feel guilty when I'm just trying to be sensible and supportive. It's best to just stick to the facts with these things, right?
Are you finding it difficult to function at work or in your daily life because of these sleep issues and feelings you're experiencing?

Difficult to function? Oh, well... I wouldn't say difficult, exactly. I mean, I'm still showing up for all the most essential meetings at the office. I would never want to leave my team in the lurch, you know? 

I suppose... well, I have had to delegate a few of my community obligations lately, and maybe I've been shortening my workdays just a little bit. But that's just because I'm not feeling quite as... steady or effective with people as I normally am, with the lack of sleep and everything. It just seemed like the responsible thing to do, to step back slightly rather than give less than my best. That makes sense, doesn't it? I'm still managing the important things, so I think I'm handling it all quite well, considering. Don't you think that's a reasonable adjustment to make for now?
How often would you say you feel this emotional numbness or distance from others?

Numbness? Oh, well... I'm not sure I'd call it numbness, exactly. That sounds so cold, doesn't it? I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm completely detached or unfeeling. 

I suppose... well, there have been a few moments. Like during the prayer gatherings for my cousin. And even when my nieces came over and really tried to comfort me. I made sure to behave properly, of course—I thanked them and said all the right things. I'd never want to seem ungrateful for their support. But... I just found myself feeling no real warmth or relief inside. It was almost as if the affectionate part of me had just... gone quiet for a little while. 

But I'm sure that's just a temporary thing, right? Just my mind trying to stay focused and strong for everyone else. I mean, it's perfectly normal to feel a little disconnected when you're trying to hold things together for the family, isn't it? I hope that doesn't make me sound terribly distant... I really am trying my best to be present for them.
How often do you find yourself feeling this way, where you don't feel any warmth or relief inside when others are trying to comfort you?

Oh, well, like I was just mentioning about the prayer gatherings and my nieces... it's really just been those few specific times. It certainly isn't a constant thing, I promise you. I wouldn't want you to think I'm walking around completely cold or unfeeling all day long. 

I think... well, in my role at the company, you really have to learn to compartmentalize to get through a crisis. So when they were trying to comfort me, my mind just sort of muted that warmth and affection so I wouldn't fall apart and make a scene. I just kept up appearances and behaved properly, like I said. So it's really only happened a handful of times since the accident, mostly when people try to get a bit too emotional with me. 

That's just a natural defense mechanism to keep functioning, don't you agree? I'm sure it's nothing to be overly concerned about, right?
For how long have you been having trouble sleeping?

Oh, the sleep... well, it hasn't been terribly long, I assure you. It's really only been about three weeks. Just since... well, since the night my cousin died in that highway collision. 

I mean, getting awful news like that, anyone would have a little trouble winding down and getting back to a normal schedule, right? It's just been those three weeks, so I'm sure my mind is just processing the shock of it all. That's a perfectly normal timeframe to be a bit restless after a family tragedy, wouldn't you say? I really don't want to make a mountain out of a molehill, and I'm sure it will pass soon enough.
Have you been feeling like you don't enjoy things as much as you used to since your cousin's death?

Oh, well... enjoy things? I suppose that's a strong way to put it. I wouldn't say I've completely lost the ability to enjoy life, certainly not. I don't want to give the impression that I'm just sitting around wallowing in misery all day. 

But... well, like I mentioned earlier about the prayer gatherings, and when my nieces came over. Usually, being around family and seeing the girls would bring me such joy, you know? I'd feel so happy to see them. But lately... I just find myself going through the motions. I smile, I make the right conversation, I behave properly... but that feeling of warmth and happiness just isn't there. It's like that affectionate, joyful part of me is just resting for a bit. 

It's not that I don't *want* to enjoy things, it's just... muted right now. But that's to be expected when you're grieving, isn't it? It doesn't mean there's something terribly wrong with me, right? I'm sure my normal sense of joy will come back once the dust settles a bit more.
How often do you feel like you're just going through the motions without really feeling anything?

Well, I suppose it's much like what I was saying just a moment ago. It really isn't an everyday occurrence, I promise you. I'd hate for you to think I'm completely hollowed out or anything like that. 

It's really just been... well, during the prayer gatherings, for instance. And even when my nieces came over and tried to comfort me. I found myself behaving properly—doing everything I was supposed to do as the head of the family—but... I just felt no warmth or relief inside. It was almost as if the affectionate part of me had just... gone quiet. 

But again, that's really only happened those few specific times when emotions were running a bit high. It's just a temporary quietness to help me cope, which makes perfect sense after a sudden shock, doesn't it? I'm sure I'm handling it the right way by just keeping it together, wouldn't you say?
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy but no longer find pleasure in since your cousin's death?

Oh, well... I suppose it really just circles back to what I was just saying, doctor. I certainly hope I don't sound like a broken record! 

As far as specific activities go, it's really just... the family events. Usually, organizing things like those prayer gatherings or having my nieces over would be the absolute highlight of my week. I take such pride and joy in hosting them, especially being the head of the family. It's something I've always loved doing.

But lately... well, exactly like I mentioned before, during the prayers, or even when the girls were sitting right there trying to comfort me... I did everything right. I behaved properly, I made sure everyone else was taken care of and comfortable. But I just didn't feel any of that usual warmth or relief inside. It's like that affectionate part of me has just gone completely quiet for the time being. 

But I'm sure that's a perfectly natural reaction, right? When you're busy making sure everyone else is holding up after a loss, you kind of have to put your own feelings on pause to be strong for them. It certainly doesn't mean I'm depressed or anything like that, wouldn't you agree? I just need a little more time to get back into the swing of things, I'm sure of it.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your ability to perform your job or maintain your social relationships since your cousin's death?

Oh, well... no, nothing terribly significant, I wouldn't say. I'm certainly not dropping the ball completely, I promise you that. My team relies on me, so I’m absolutely still showing up for all the most essential meetings. I make sure the important things are handled just like always. 

But... I suppose I have made a few small adjustments, just temporarily. I've had to delegate some of my usual community obligations to my staff, and... well, I have been shortening my workdays just a little bit lately. It's really only because I've noticed I'm just not quite as steady or... effective with people as I normally am. I pride myself on being very present for my team, and if I'm not at my absolute best, I'd rather let someone else take the reins for a moment.

Taking a small step back and delegating is the responsible thing to do when you're going through something like this, don't you think? It shows good leadership to pace yourself rather than push too hard and make mistakes, right?
How often do you feel like you're just going through the motions without feeling any emotions at all?

Oh... well, I feel like we might be circling back to the same sort of thing again, doctor. I do hope I'm making sense and not just repeating myself too much. 

But really, as I was saying before, it's not an everyday thing. I'm definitely not walking around completely numb all the time, I promise you. I still feel things, of course I do. It's truly just been those specific moments I mentioned—the prayer gatherings, or when my nieces were here. Those were the times when I noticed I was just... doing what needed to be done, without that usual warmth. 

But outside of those moments where I really had to be strong for the family, I don't feel like I'm just going through the motions at all. I'm still very much present and engaged in my life, even with delegating a few things at work. I think it's just a matter of compartmentalizing when I need to, which is a very healthy way to manage things, wouldn't you say? It's just a normal part of holding everything together, right?
For how many weeks have you been feeling like the affectionate part of you has gone quiet?

Oh, let me think... I suppose it's been right around three weeks now. Yes, just about three weeks, ever since the night my cousin passed away in that... well, in that highway collision. 

But three weeks really isn't a very long time at all to process something like that, is it? I mean, anyone would need at least a few weeks to get their bearings after a sudden shock, don't you think? It seems like a perfectly reasonable amount of time to still be feeling just a little out of sorts, wouldn't you agree? I'm sure I'll be completely back to my old self before too long.
Are there things you usually enjoy doing that you have stopped doing since your cousin's death?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I've stopped doing things I enjoy. Not at all. I mean, I'm still keeping up with my usual routine for the most part. 

I suppose I haven't been quite as... active with my weekend gardening club as I usually am, but that's really just because the weather hasn't been ideal, and I've had so much family business to attend to. And I did skip my Wednesday evening book club last week, but I hadn't finished the chapters anyway, so it just made sense to sit that one out. 

I'm certainly not isolating myself or giving up my hobbies, I promise you. I'm just prioritizing where my energy needs to go right now, which is completely understandable under the circumstances, don't you think? It's just a matter of being practical for a few weeks, right?
For how long have you been feeling like you're going through the motions without feeling any emotions?

Oh, well, I suppose that would be the exact same timeframe, doctor. Like I mentioned just a moment ago—and I do hope I'm answering these correctly for you, I know we're covering similar ground—it's been right about three weeks. Ever since the night of my cousin's highway collision. 

But again, I really don't want you to think I've just been walking around completely blank for three weeks straight! It truly is just during those specific times when I've had to step up and manage the family affairs. Anyone would need to put their feelings aside for a few weeks to handle all the logistics after a shock like that, wouldn't they? It's just a sensible, practical way to cope in the short term while everyone else is grieving, right?
Do you feel sad most of the day, nearly every day?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. Not most of the day, and certainly not every day. I mean, of course I have moments where I feel a little down—anyone would, given what happened with my cousin, don't you think? It's only natural to have a few tears here and there when you lose someone. 

But I'm really not sitting around crying all day or anything like that. I've been keeping quite busy, actually. I make sure to get up and dressed every morning, and I'm still handling my responsibilities at work. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just wallowing in it. It's just a perfectly normal, manageable amount of sadness for the situation, wouldn't you agree? I'm handling it as well as anyone could be expected to.
Do you feel sad most of the day?

Well, like I was just saying... no, not most of the day. I know we just touched on this, and I hope I'm being clear enough for you. I really don't feel that heavy, constant sadness that you're asking about. 

I mean, I'm keeping my chin up, going to the office, making sure the company is running smoothly. A chief executive can't really afford to be sad all day, you know? People are counting on me. So, no, it's definitely not most of the day. Just... just the normal, fleeting moments of missing him. That's exactly how I should be handling it, right? Staying strong and keeping things moving?
